question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Six months — an officer or employee who wishes to "opt out of employment in the Institute" may do so "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [621/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- The offer itself is to be made with effect from the date of commencement of the Act, on terms "not less favorable" than those existing the day before [621/2025 §33(2)(a)].
- Anyone who declines is paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme, approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [621/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: the quoted wording is from the GS version 621/2025 (published 2025-07-17); the evidence indicates identical text appears in 629/2025 (Bill, 2025-08-19) but the clause text of that Bill's §33 is not itself reproduced here.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded for “any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018” [013/2026 §37].

- This applies even if an un-deducted balance of that deduction remains as at April 1, 2018 [013/2026 §37].
- Source: Inland Revenue (Amendment) – GS, published 24 February 2026; identical text appears in 022/2026 [013/2026 §37].

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is “valid for a period of one year” and must specify its expiry date [645/2025 §25(c),(d)].

- A separate licence to carry on the **microfinance business** is stated to be “issued for a period of three years” [645/2025 §32(7)].

Caveat: the Bill is internally inconsistent depending on which licence is meant; the text is from the GS dated 2025-11-17 [645/2025].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
Under the newest text, **Bill 033/2026 (2026‑05‑05)**, the long-stop maximum is raised from “a period of two years” to **“a period of three years”** [033/2026 §9]. The same amendment also raises a separate limit from “shall not exceed three months” to **“shall not exceed four months”** [033/2026 §9].

- The police-issued Freezing Order period is changed from “seven days” to **“fourteen working days”** [033/2026 §8].
- The earlier GS version, **020/2026 (2026‑03‑17)**, has identical wording [020/2026 §9].

Caveats: The evidence does not include the principal Act, so the precise operation of the “three months/four months” and “two years/three years” limits within section 8(2) is not fully shown.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
Monthly — the levy is charged on the value of the supply "in respect of each month" [028/2026 §2].

- The charge is levied on every person receiving a telecommunication service, at the rate specified in the Schedule, on the value of supply by any operator or provider [028/2026 §2].
- Diplomatic Privileges Act No. 9 of 1996 persons/organisations are exempt [028/2026 §2].
- Same clause text appears in the presented Bill 035/2026 (2026-05-06); the GS version is 028/2026 (2026-04-23) [035/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence does not state the current rate, only that it is set in the Schedule.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amended section 49(5) allows notice of dishonour to be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" that sufficiently identify the bill and intimate dishonour [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic route is conditional: the means must "sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [601/2025 §8].
- Text is identical across the 2025 and 2024 versions (GS 601/2025, 4 Jun 2025; Bill 612/2025, 17 Jun 2025) [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: Only the substituted subsection (5) is quoted; the rest of section 49 is not in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
The one passage carrying the Kodhagoda title — [626/2025 §11] — defines "qualified auditor" as either (a) an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or any other institute established by law, and "possesses a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute", or (b) a firm of Accountants whose resident partners each meet that membership and certificate requirement [626/2025 §11(4)].

- The same clause says the accounts "shall be audited by a qualified auditor appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].
- Similar boilerplate appears in other bills, e.g. [547/2024 §11(4)], [114/2021 §8(3)].

Caveats: that passage's text is garbled (stray headings, "certified" for "certificate") and should not be treated as the settled wording; no clean Kodhagoda audit/definition clause is in the evidence, so the exact enacted definition is missing. This is not legal advice.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
Under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) bill, "knowledge sharing activities" means "activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration" [646/2025 §18].

- This is the definition clause ("In this Act, unless the context otherwise required"), so the term carries this meaning throughout the Act [646/2025 §18].
- The same text appears in bill 002/2026; the evidence is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-11-20), p.15 [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: The quoted wording is reproduced verbatim from the bill, including its drafting slips ("facilitate to exchange", "fostering on culture"); no other clause elaborating on the term is in the evidence.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
Under the newest version, the Bill cited as the Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka (Incorporation) Bill [047/2026], dated 2026-06-25, the Society may "take and hold any property, movable or immovable" and hold it for the purposes of the Act, subject to its rules [047/2026 §13].

- It may obtain property by "purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise", with power to "sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same" [047/2026 §13].
- It may buy, rent, construct or renovate lands or buildings and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may administer "any lawful trust" or "real or personal property" promoting its objects [047/2026 §6(f)]; property management is also a matter for rules [047/2026 §7(1)(f)].

Caveats: The earlier Gazette version [041/2026 §§6, 13], dated 2026-06-11, uses identical wording; no difference appears in these passages.

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs both: the "Membership Committee" and the "Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee" [656/2025 §18(2)] (same text in the earlier GS version [637/2025 §18(2)]).

- Other committees must include at least one Council member, and that member is the Chairman [656/2025 §18(2)].
- If more than one Council member is appointed to a committee, the Council appoints one of them as Chairperson [656/2025 §18(3)].
- In a Chairperson's absence, members present elect one of themselves to preside [656/2025 §18(5)].

Caveats: The bill titles the second body "Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee"; both GS (2025-10-01) and Bill (2025-12-05) texts are identical here.

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the amended law, workers of businesses licensed **before** the new section commences get a three-year income-tax exemption; workers of businesses licensed **on or after** commencement are taxable. The same substituted section 35 appears in Bill 654/2025 (2025-12-05) and GS 652/2025 (2025-11-28).

- Pre-commencement licensees: for “a period of three years”, resident employees’ “employment income” is “exempt from income tax” and deemed a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account [654/2025 §3].
- Pre-commencement licensees: non-resident employees’ employment income is also “exempt from income tax”, and they are not liable to Sri Lanka income tax on income earned outside Sri Lanka [654/2025 §3].
- Post-commencement licensees: “employment income” of resident and non-resident employees “shall be liable to income tax” [654/2025 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment removes “container operators” from the 1972 Act’s long title by substituting “freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers” for “freight forwarders, non-vessel operating common carriers, and container operators” [658/2025 §2].

- This is the same in the later Bill 005/2026 (2026-01-20); the GS version is 658/2025 (2025-12-12) [658/2025 §2].
- The substituted wording omits “and container operators” entirely [658/2025 §2].

Caveats: The full clause text is quoted from 658/2025 §2, which the evidence says is identical in 005/2026.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The newest version is Bill 029/2026 (2026‑04‑09), whose text is identical to GS 018/2026 (2026‑03‑11); it amends the 2005 Act in several sections rather than by one change. Key modifications to section 3: a new proviso that it "shall not be necessary to show" the funds were "actually used" or linked to a specific terrorist act [029/2026 §4], plus new conduct offences — "organizes and directs", "participates as an accomplice", "contributes to" [029/2026 §4].

- Section 2A is replaced so the Act reaches acts committed "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" targeting Sri Lanka, its citizens, government facilities, or to compel the Government [029/2026 §3].
- Section 4E tracing/document powers are widened to "funds, property or other assets" [029/2026 §9].

Caveats: no passage states the amendment's overall purpose; the evidence is incomplete on that integrated overview.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The **Appropriation Bill 639/2025** (Bill, presented 2025-09-26) — its text is identical to 632/2025 (published 2025-09-17).

- It authorises "rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand" for the "financial year 2026" (1 Jan–31 Dec 2026) [639/2025 §2(1)].
- Borrowing is authorised in or outside Sri Lanka, capped so the balance outstanding "shall not exceed rupees three thousand eight hundred billion", with loan details in the Final Budget Position Report under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act No. 44 of 2024 [639/2025 §2(1)].
- Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund is estimated at "rupees four thousand five hundred forty-five billion six hundred forty-three million five hundred thirty-two thousand" [639/2025 §2(4)].

Caveats: The amounts above are drawn from the shared §2 text; the bill-level summaries are auto-generated hints only.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
It is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** Bill — Bill **055/2026** (presented 27 July 2026), with an earlier Gazette version, **043/2026** (published 15 June 2026).

- It declares the body corporate's objects to include contributing "to national and social development by developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" [043/2026 §3(1)(a)].
- It covers "human resource development programmes" for "rural youth and adult community", and empowering "rural, estate and underserved communities" [043/2026 §3(1)(b), (h)].
- It incorporates existing members with perpetual succession, deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [043/2026 §2].

Caveats: The 055/2026 title spells "Recourses"; §3 text is identical in both versions per the evidence. No penalties are set out.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year** — the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member," "warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

- The suspension power arises once the Disciplinary Committee's report establishes "professional misconduct" [054/2026 §24], as defined by Council rules under section 26 [054/2026 §23].
- The Council may also re-enroll the person at its discretion if it considers them fit [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: the same text appears in bills 040/2026 and 050/2026; amendments made at committee stage are not covered here.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, a person must have been in **“undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation”** of the premises for **“a period of more than three months”**, prior to the events in sections 3, 4 or 5, and also be in lawful occupation [004/2026 §2].

- The same threshold appears in the earlier Gazette version: more than three months [634/2025 §2].
- Newest evidence is Bill 004/2026 (2026-01-20); GS 634/2025 is dated 2025-09-18 [004/2026 §2; 634/2025 §2].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The evidence states a person is disqualified from being appointed to the Board if he "is over seventy years of age" — i.e., 70 is the threshold. This appears in both versions of the Gambling Regulatory Authority bill (594/2025 GS, 27 May 2025; 613/2025 Bill, 17 June 2025), with identical wording.

- Disqualification is framed as a bar on appointment, listed among other grounds: "[613/2025 §9]... (i) is over seventy years of age"; same at [594/2025 §9].
- The list is introduced as grounds on which "[a] person shall be disqualified from being appointed as a member of the Board" [613/2025 §9; 594/2025 §9].

Caveats: The clause addresses appointment only — the evidence does not show a separate rule on ceasing to hold office on reaching that age; the two bills' §9 text is identical, so no GS/Bill difference arises.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The longest jail term is **one year**: conviction by a Magistrate carries “imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year” [021/2026 §31].

- The same provision also allows a fine “not exceeding three times of the value” of the cash or instruments, or both fine and imprisonment [021/2026 §31].
- The excess cash or bearer-negotiable instruments are forfeited to the State [021/2026 §31].

Caveats: This is the Gazette version of the Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) bill (2026-03-17); the evidence says the text is identical in 030/2026, and committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the Sri Lanka Cricket bill, a member who misses the subscription deadline owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- Deadline for the annual subscription: on or before "the thirty first day of December of the year immediately preceding the relevant year" [072/2026 §30(3)].
- The doubled fee is payable "on or before the thirtieth day of April of the following year" [072/2026 §30(4)].
- If still unpaid by that date, the member "shall automatically forfeit its voting right", and removal from the Register follows after six months [072/2026 §30(5)–(6)].

Caveats: this is the GS version (2026-09-28); the same text appears in 077/2026. The bill-level summary is auto-generated, so figures above are from the clause text.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The clause fixes *which* debts, not a payment deadline: those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" must be paid by the body corporate — no day for settlement is stated [009/2026 §12].

- Newest matching bill: "Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation)" — GS, 2026-02-05; identical text in 014/2026 [009/2026 §12].
- Older "Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation)" — GS, 2021-08-23 — uses the same wording [095/2021 §12].
- Amounts due to the Trust on that day are likewise payable to the body corporate [009/2026 §12].

Caveats: No payment date or time limit appears in the evidence; the bill title differs slightly from the name in your question.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under §90 of the Immigration Bill (082/2026, Bill dated 2026-10-07), the penalty is a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than five hundred thousand rupees" [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The offence is failing to notify an Immigration Officer that a transit passenger or crew member did not continue his journey [082/2026 §90(1)–(2)]; master, captain and agent are "jointly and severally liable" [082/2026 §90(2)].
- Don't confuse this with the separate removal/receiving-on-board offence under §89, which carries "not less than five hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees" per person [082/2026 §89(3)].

Caveats: The same §90 text appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026; the figure quoted is from the 2026-10-07 Bill version.

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
Three years, with eligibility for reappointment — stated in the newest version, the Bill [636/2025 §11] (12 Sept 2025), and identically in the earlier Gazette version [631/2025 §11] (4 Sept 2025).

- The Minister appoints one of the "appointed members" as Chairman "on the recommendation of the majority decision of the ex-officio members" [636/2025 §11].
- "The Chairman so appointed shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for reappointment" [636/2025 §11].

Caveats: The two 2025 texts are identical on this point; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus. The 2013 Act [044/2013 §14] also had a three-year term.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The new definition, substituted in s.52 of the principal Act, is: ““Director-General” means the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [595/2025 §6] (identical text also in 620/2025, the Bill dated 2025-07-09; the GS version 595/2025 is dated 2025-05-28).

- The substitution replaces the repealed definition of “Controller” [595/2025 §6].
- Relatedly, references to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in the Act become “Director-General” [620/2025 §2], and in other laws/documents are read as “Director-General of the Rubber Development Department” [620/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: none; §6 text is confirmed only in the GS version, stated as identical in the Bill.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
The evidence I have does not contain a definition of "public authority" — the definitions passage is truncated before that term, so I cannot state which bodies are included.

- The definition section excerpt runs only up to "financial data" and defines "controller" as including a "public authority" without defining it [152/2021 §47].
- Elsewhere the draft refers to processing "carried out by a ministry, government department or public corporation" as the trigger for appointing a Data Protection Officer [152/2021 §20(1)(a)], and to "a public authority" processing as controller or processor being restricted to processing in Sri Lanka [152/2021 §26(1)] — but neither passage says these bodies are "regarded as" a public authority.

Caveats: The text I have is the 2021 Gazette draft, *Personal Data Protection* [152/2021, GS 2021-11-25], not an "amended Act"; I have no later amendment text. The definition of "public authority" (and any related definitions such as "public corporation") is missing from the evidence.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
The crop must have "export potential in addition to the local consumption", be excluded from the listed food-crop categories, not be a plantation crop, and be declared by the Minister as "a notified agricultural crop" under section 2 [045/2026 §5] (noted there as identical in 060/2026, the newer Bill of 2026-08-07; the GS version is 045/2026 of 2026-06-25).

- Excluded: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops" [045/2026 §5].
- Also "shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop" [045/2026 §5].
- The Minister's declaration is the operative step, made under section 2 of the principal Act [045/2026 §5].

Caveats: Only the GS clause text is quoted; the 060/2026 Bill text is described as identical at bill level.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the Chiththa bill, “qualified auditor” means either an individual member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute established by law) holding a certificate to practise as an Accountant issued by that institute’s Council, or a firm of Accountants whose resident partners each meet that same requirement [597/2025 §10(4)].

- The auditor is appointed by the Auditor General under Article 154 of the Constitution [597/2025 §10(3)].
- The definition is set out in the same section, using “means” — so the categories appear exhaustive [597/2025 §10(4)(a)–(b)].

Caveats: This is the GS version (published 2025-05-29, also reproduced in 608/2025); no presented Bill version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Bill, the listed “advanced investigative techniques” are controlled delivery; digital surveillance, including interception/recording of digital, voice and video communications; undercover operations including decoys; traps; and forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, phones and other digital devices, subject to Magistrate authorisation [570/2025 §60].

- The Magistrate must consider “necessity and justification” and proportionality, and may impose conditions [570/2025 §60].
- Progress must be reported to the Magistrate “once in fourteen days” [570/2025 §60].
- The Bill’s §61 separately allows judicial orders for forensic audits, digital forensic extraction, valuation, copying/storing data, and forensic transaction analysis [572/2025 §61].

Caveats: The explicit “advanced investigative techniques” list is in the GS version, 570/2025 §60; the evidence states that text is identical in Bill 572/2025.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and the Chairperson must be one of them: "the quorum... shall be five members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7(2)] (Bill, 22 July 2026; the identical GS version is [040/2026 §7(2)], 5 June 2026).

- Meetings may also be held by audio-visual means, provided all members forming the quorum can simultaneously see and hear each other [054/2026 §7(3)(b)].
- Decisions are by majority of members present and voting, with the Chairperson holding a casting vote on an equality of votes [054/2026 §7(4)].

Caveats: §7(5)(b) lets the Vice-Chairperson preside if the Chairperson is absent, which sits awkwardly with the Chairperson-inclusive quorum; no amendment resolving this appears in the evidence.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under the National Transport Commission (Amendment) Bill [592/2025 §19] (new s.38A), the Commission computes fares by a formula it determines, adhering to Parliament-approved national fare policy, and specifies them by Gazette Order; it then publishes fare lists on its website, and each provider must prepare its own list accordingly and display it conspicuously on the vehicle.

- Formula must follow stakeholder written representations and be revised periodically [592/2025 §5(o)].
- Commission may inspect compliance; non-compliance is "guilty of an offence under section 40" [592/2025 §19; 577/2025 §19].
- Same text appears in the earlier GS version [577/2025 §19, 2025-04-07].

Caveats: The quoted s.38A(3) text is truncated/garbled in the evidence, and the penalty under s.40 is not stated here.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
In Bill 037/2026 (2026-05-07; identical wording in GS 025/2026, 2026-04-08), the Foundation has “perpetual succession” under the name “Mass Foundation” and “may sue and be sued” [037/2026 §2].

- It may “have and use a common seal” and “alter the same at its pleasure” [037/2026 §2].
- The seal may be affixed only in the presence of two Committee members who sign independently, and is kept in the custody of a Committee office bearer as the Committee decides [037/2026 §15].
- It is “deemed to be a Voluntary Social Service Organization” under the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration and Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to its management [037/2026 §2].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Under Bill **053/2026** (newest, 21 July 2026; identical in 019/2026), for an industrial estate or industrial park the reference is to “the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka … or the Minister assigned the subject of industries … as the case may be” [053/2026 §10; 019/2026 §10].

- This replaces “the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” for Part III purposes in that scenario [053/2026 §10].

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (Bill, 2026-10-06), the magistrate with jurisdiction over an approved place of detention must, without any advance notice to the authority in charge, visit it monthly, interview suspects and look into their well-being, and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other required documents [078/2026 §33(1)].

- If torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment is observed or alleged, he "shall forthwith make an order" for production before a Judicial Medical Officer and submission of the report [078/2026 §33(4)].
- If satisfied on reasonable grounds after hearing the suspect and police officer, he "shall act in terms of section 31" (medical treatment, JMO examination, change of detention place) [078/2026 §33(5), §31].
- Non-conforming conditions found at inspection must be informed to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: The same text appears in 070/2026; dates for that version are not in the evidence.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
Under Bill 622/2025 (Bill, 2025-07-11; the earlier GS 616/2025 of 2025-07-03 carries identical text on these points), mediation covers "civil and commercial disputes" — whether under a mediation agreement, referred voluntarily by a party, or referred by a court [622/2025 §2(1)].

- Excluded: disputes to be mediated under the Mediation Boards Act No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act No. 21 of 2003 [622/2025 §2(2)–(3)].
- Excluded: disputes whose settlement needs terms enforceable only by court decree/order, including the scheduled list — divorce and nullity, persons of unsound mind/minors/wards, guardians, adoption, births and deaths, partition for rights in rem, probate, insolvency, admiralty rights in rem, and fundamental-rights breaches [622/2025 §3; §30 schedule].
- Related matters may still be mediated to submit settlement terms to court [622/2025 §3 proviso].

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
New section 35A requires the accounts of **samurdhi community based banking societies** to be audited under Article 154 of the Constitution (public corporation audit provisions) and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 [600/2025 §3].

- The same rules are applied separately to "samurdhi community based banks" by the new section 28A [600/2025 §2].
- Both insertions appear in the GS version of 2025-06-04 (600/2025) and are stated to be identical in the Bill version of 2025-06-17 (614/2025) [600/2025 §3; 614/2025].

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
Under the 2026 amendments to section 149, all offences become "cognizable and non-bailable", but bail is refused outright only in the threshold cases below, and then only a High Court may grant it "in exceptional circumstances".

- Bribe of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees" solicited, accepted or offered [063/2026 §17]; same in the earlier Gazette version [051/2026 §17].
- Corruption causing Government loss, or gain/benefit/favour/advantage to himself or another, of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees", value "confirmed by the Director-General by issuing a certificate" [063/2026 §17].
- Then: "such suspect or accused shall not be granted bail except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" [063/2026 §17].

Caveats: Both versions are amendments to s.149; the Bill text [063/2026] contains a garbled phrase ("offering of section 149 of the principal enactment a bribe") absent from the GS [051/2026]. The evidence does not reproduce the Act's other bail provisions, so the full position on refusal of bail is missing.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under §11, such Part B offences are deemed **not** to be “an offence of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives” for extradition purposes — notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977 [073/2026 §11].

- The deeming applies “for the purposes only of extradition” of a person accused or convicted of such an offence, “as between the Government of Sri Lanka and any UN Member State”, and for assistance under section 12 [073/2026 §11].
- Related machinery: existing extradition arrangements with UN Member States are deemed to include the Act's offences [073/2026 §9], and the Minister must notify a requesting State of measures taken [073/2026 §10].

Caveats: The text appears identically in the later presented version, Bill 085/2026 (Bill, 2026-10-20), per the evidence labels; 073/2026 is the GS version (2026-09-30).

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the revised National Environmental Act, a Section 23r offence carries a fine of “not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees” on conviction, plus “five thousand rupees for each day” the offence continues after conviction [032/2026 §18].

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:

- Penalty: fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [068/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 006/2026 — the **Rent (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20) — provides that "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].

- The bill is titled as repealing the **Rent Act**, No. 7 of 1972, not a "Tenancy Act", though it is plainly the Act in question [006/2026 §2].
- Transitional protections run "for a period of one year from the relevant date": no ejectment actions against tenants and no rent above the "authorised rent" [006/2026 §3(a)–(b)].
- Pending Rent Board and Board of Review matters must be "proceeded with and concluded within a period of one year" [006/2026 §3(d)–(e)].

Caveats: The earlier Rent (Repeal) GS of 2024-07-19 (526/2024) has identical operative text; only the 2026 Bill version is dated this year.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
Bill 015/2026, the **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)** Bill (presented 2026-02-18), which incorporates the existing centre as a body corporate with perpetual succession, power to sue and be sued, and a common seal [015/2026 §2].

- Its Gazette predecessor, GS 011/2026 (2026-02-06), contains identical clause text [011/2026 §2].
- The corporation is deemed a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [011/2026 §2(2)].
- Objects include IT-related training and skills programmes for rural youth [011/2026 §3].

Caveats: Titles vary slightly between the short title and the corporate name ("Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children") [011/2026 §2]; summaries are auto-generated hints only.
